data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'Lydia', meaning 'woman from Lydia'. In the New Testament, Lydia was a woman from Thyatira who was a seller of purple and a worshiper of God. She was the first European convert to Christianity. The name Lydie carries the meaning “Lady, Woman” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Lydie usually hope their child will grow to embody lady, woman and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Lydie total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_hebrew.name: לידיה
in_hebrew.meaning: עובדת האל, שירתה את האל, מעובדת אלוהים
in_hebrew.long_meaning: לידיה הוא שם שמקורו ביוונית ולידית, שפירושו עובדת האל או שירתה את האל. זהו שם שמיוחס לנשים ששירתו את אלוהים ופעלו למען הדת הנוצרית. השם לידיה מוזכר בברית החדשה, בספר מעשי השליחים, כהשם של אישה ששירתה את האל וסייעה לשליח פאולוס ושותפיו בהפצת הבשורה.

in_greek.name: Λυδία
in_greek.long_meaning: Λυδία ὁ Λυδός ἀπὸ τῆς Λυδίας, ἡ ἀδελφή ἡ ἀγάπη, ἡ δοχή τοῦ Θεοῦ. Τὸ ὄνομα Λυδία προέρχεται ἀπὸ τὴν περιοχή Λυδία τῆς Μικράς Ἀσίας καὶ σημαίνει ἡ ἀδελφή ἡ δοχή.

in_latin.name: Lydia
in_latin.meaning: beautiful one, lovely, worker of God
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Lydia is derived from the Greek region of Lydia, and it means beautiful one, lovely, or worker of God. In Christian tradition, Lydia is associated with a woman from Thyatira who was a seller of purple fabrics and became one of the first converts to Christianity in Europe, as recorded in the Acts of the Apostles.

in_english.name: Lydie
in_english.meaning: Beautiful, lovely, or worker of God
in_english.long_meaning: The name Lydie is of Greek origin, derived from the region of Lydia in Asia Minor. It means beautiful, lovely, or worker of God. In Christian tradition, Lydia is a significant name due to its association with a woman from Thyatira who became a follower of Jesus Christ and played a crucial role in the early Christian church. The name symbolizes beauty, spirituality, and devotion to God.

data.cultural_impact: In the Middle Ages, the name Lydie gained popularity in France, and it became common among the French-speaking population. It was often given to girls born into noble families or to those who were destined for a life of luxury. Today, Lydie is a popular name in France, Belgium, and Canada.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Lydie has a significant spiritual connection to the early Christian Church. Lydia was a prominent woman who played a crucial role in the spread of Christianity in Europe. Her conversion not only marked the beginning of Christianity in Europe but also paved the way for many other converts. Therefore, the name Lydie serves as a reminder of the early Christian Church, faith, and the important role women played in its growth.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Lydie carries profound spiritual symbolism as it is rooted in Biblical tradition.
